lessons.title: Exercise 9 - Questions 9.25 to 9.29
lessons.notes_html:
Q9.25 Five balls are drawn from a box containing 4 white and 7 black balls. If X is the number of black balls drawn, find the distribution of X, its mean and variance, and verify the mean and variance by formula.

Step 1: The drawing is without replacement, so X follows a hypergeometric distribution. The total number of selections is C(11, 5) = 462.

Step 2: P(X = 1) = C(7, 1) times C(4, 4) divided by 462 = 7/462 = 1/66.

Step 3: P(X = 2) = C(7, 2) times C(4, 3) divided by 462 = 84/462 = 12/66.

Step 4: P(X = 3) = C(7, 3) times C(4, 2) divided by 462 = 210/462 = 30/66.

Step 5: P(X = 4) = C(7, 4) times C(4, 1) divided by 462 = 140/462 = 20/66.

Step 6: P(X = 5) = C(7, 5) times C(4, 0) divided by 462 = 21/462 = 3/66.

Step 7: Mean = (1 times 7 + 2 times 84 + 3 times 210 + 4 times 140 + 5 times 21) divided by 462 = 1470/462 = 35/11 = 3.1818. By formula, mean = n times K divided by N = 5 times 7 divided by 11 = 35/11.

Step 8: E(X^2) = (1 times 7 + 4 times 84 + 9 times 210 + 16 times 140 + 25 times 21) divided by 462 = 4998/462 = 10.8182, so variance = 10.8182 - (35/11)^2 = 0.6942. By formula, variance = n times (K/N) times (1 - K/N) times ((N - n)/(N - 1)) = 5 times (7/11) times (4/11) times (6/10) = 0.6942.

Answer: Distribution 1/66, 12/66, 30/66, 20/66, 3/66; Mean = 35/11; Variance = 0.6942, verified by formula.

Q9.26 A box contains 4 white and 7 black beads. Five beads are drawn at random. Find the distribution of the number of white beads drawn, its mean and variance, and check them by formula.

Step 1: The drawing is without replacement, so the number of white beads follows a hypergeometric distribution with N = 11, K = 4 white beads and n = 5 draws. Total selections = C(11, 5) = 462.

Step 2: P(X = 0) = C(4, 0) times C(7, 5) divided by 462 = 21/462.

Step 3: P(X = 1) = C(4, 1) times C(7, 4) divided by 462 = 140/462.

Step 4: P(X = 2) = C(4, 2) times C(7, 3) divided by 462 = 210/462.

Step 5: P(X = 3) = C(4, 3) times C(7, 2) divided by 462 = 84/462.

Step 6: P(X = 4) = C(4, 4) times C(7, 1) divided by 462 = 7/462.

Step 7: Mean = (0 times 21 + 1 times 140 + 2 times 210 + 3 times 84 + 4 times 7) divided by 462 = 840/462 = 1.8181. By formula, mean = n times K divided by N = 5 times 4 divided by 11 = 1.8181.

Step 8: Variance = 0.6942, the same value as in Question 9.25 (white and black counts are complementary). By formula, variance = 5 times (4/11) times (7/11) times (6/10) = 0.6942.

Answer: Distribution 21/462, 140/462, 210/462, 84/462, 7/462; Mean = 1.8181; Variance = 0.6942, verified by formula.

Q9.27 A committee of 3 is to be formed from 4 men and 2 women. Find the hypergeometric distribution of the number of men on the committee.

Step 1: Total selections = C(6, 3) = 20.

Step 2: P(X = 1) = C(4, 1) times C(2, 2) divided by 20 = 4/20.

Step 3: P(X = 2) = C(4, 2) times C(2, 1) divided by 20 = 12/20.

Step 4: P(X = 3) = C(4, 3) times C(2, 0) divided by 20 = 4/20.

Answer: X = 1, 2, 3 with probabilities 4/20, 12/20, 4/20.

Q9.28 A committee of 5 is chosen from 3 women and 5 men. Find the expected number of women on the committee.

The committee has 5 members chosen from 3 women and 5 men. The expected number of women is 5 times 3 divided by 8 = 15/8 = 1.875.

Q9.29 Ten vegetable cans, 5 of tomatoes and 5 of corns, are placed in a box and 5 are selected at random. Find the probability that (i) all contain tomatoes, (ii) 3 or more contain tomatoes.

Step 1: Total selections = C(10, 5) = 252.

Step 2: (i) P(all 5 are tomatoes) = C(5, 5) divided by 252 = 1/252.

Step 3: (ii) P(3 or more tomatoes) = P(3) + P(4) + P(5) = (100 + 25 + 1) divided by 252 = 126/252.

Answer: (i) 1/252, (ii) 126/252.

lessons.title: Exercise 9 - Note on the Answers key
lessons.notes_html:
Note on the Answers key

Note on the book's printed Answers key (p. 261): the key marks 9.30 (i) F, (vii) F, (viii) T, (x) T. The answers given here follow the chapter's definitions, and differ from the key at four places. (i) An experiment with exactly two possible outcomes is a Bernoulli experiment, so the statement is True. (vii) When p > q, that is p > 1/2, the binomial distribution is negatively skewed, so the statement is True. (viii) The hypergeometric distribution comes from sampling without replacement, so its trials are not independent, and the statement is False. (x) The binomial distribution applies for any fixed n; a large n is the condition for the normal approximation, not for the binomial distribution itself, so the statement is False. The four key entries are treated as misprints.

Note on 9.16: the printed key (p. 260) gives mean 40 and standard deviation 6. The question in 9.16 states a total of 500 bolts with defective probability 0.1, so the mean is 500 times 0.1 = 50 and the standard deviation is the square root of 500 times 0.1 times 0.9 = 6.71. The key's values 40 and 6 are the values for a total of 400, not 500, and are treated as misprints.
